name: Almaty International Airport
before:
Kazakhstan's main international gateway and the busiest airport in Central Asia, larger than the airport at the capital. It is the principal hub of Air Astana and handled 7.2 million passengers in 2022, roughly two thirds of them on domestic routes.

Terminal 2 is the thing that has changed here. It opened in June 2024, handles international flights only, and covers more than 53,000 square metres with 50 check in counters, 20 passport control booths and four automated e-gates. It sits north east of Terminal 1 and is joined to it by an indoor bridge, so a domestic to international connection stays under cover. Between them the terminals lift the airport's capacity to 14 million passengers a year.

There is a small museum inside Terminal 2 covering the airport's history, alongside the duty free and VIP lounges.

Terminal 1 dates from December 2003, rebuilt after a fire in 1999.

Bus routes 3 and 92 stop in front of both terminals, and Yandex Taxi operates here alongside ordinary taxis. The airport is owned by the Turkish operator TAV.
